answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation updates. A challenger earns part of that stake only by proving fraud, while honest agents recover theirs after a fixed period; reputation changes then use stake-weighted votes rather than raw account counts. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must immobilize real capital for every fake identity and risks losing it when caught. A karst network, orchard registry, or vertex community can all apply the same rule.
